title: When the Smile Breaks
premise: Hospice nurse Oscar Winterbourne has spent his career dismissing the dying's habit of counting backwards from ten, chalking it up to terminal lucidity. When an excavation crew on the edge of Hollowmere unearths a door sealed from the inside, the town's oldest families begin counting too — and the crew members who opened the door start disappearing one by one as their counts reach zero. Oscar must abandon his rationalism and lead the surviving family of the door's original keepers through a ritual of return before the harvest moon rises, learning that justice was never delivered to what lies beneath Hollowmere, only buried. In the end, Oscar takes the dead family's place at the threshold, sealing it from the inside so the count can finally stop — trading his survival for the town's belonging.
about_author: Tamsin Blackwood is the pen name of a former palliative care volunteer who spent six years listening to the last words of the dying in rural England. She writes horror about the debts communities owe their dead, and lives near the moors she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Ten
chapters.summary: Oscar Winterbourne, POV. At Marlowe Hospice, elderly Edith Garrick counts backwards from ten and dies exactly on zero — the fourth patient that month. Oscar documents it clinically, refusing pattern or meaning. His colleague Priya begs him to see what he's seeing. Emotional beat: the comfort of denial established as a fortress with hairline cracks.

chapters.title: The Door Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: Crew foreman Danny Okafor, POV. The excavation crew breaks ground on the old Winterbourne land and strikes a stone door with no handle, its hinges rusted shut — from within. Danny touches it and hears ten soft knocks. That night his daughter says there's a man under her bed counting. Emotional beat: dread arriving through domestic innocence.

chapters.title: Nine
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Patients across Hollowmere begin counting in unison, wards apart, hours apart. Priya shows him census records: every counting death matches a name from the 1847 disappearances of the Vane family, the town's founding keepers. Oscar's own surname appears in the ledger. Emotional beat: denial curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: What the Town Buried
chapters.summary: Mabel Vane, 91, last of the keeper line, POV. Mabel confesses the family covenant: in 1847 the Vanes walled something in their cellar alive to end a plague, and the count is its ledger of what it's owed. She gives Oscar the iron key and the rite of return. Emotional beat: inherited guilt as inheritance itself.

chapters.title: Eight
chapters.summary: Danny, POV. Two crewmen vanish; their tents hold only clocks stopped at zero. The door has begun breathing — frost exhaling from its seams. Danny's daughter draws the door perfectly, down to scratches no one has seen. Emotional beat: the horror stops being historical and becomes parental terror.

chapters.title: Seven, Six, Five
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The whole town counts now, in sleep, in shops, in church. Priya's count begins. Oscar realizes the rite requires the Vane bloodline to walk the family out ahead of the count before the full harvest moon — but Mabel is dying, counting, and cannot walk. Emotional beat: the plan collapsing under the weight of time.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises Early
chapters.summary: Priya, POV, fading. Clouds part days early; the moon rises fat and orange over Hollowmere. The door opens inward by itself. What comes out wears the faces of the vanished crew, smiling wrong. Priya holds the threshold with her last counted breaths so Oscar can reach Mabel. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof that belief was never the price — action was.

chapters.title: Four, Three, Two
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. With Mabel dying in his arms, Oscar learns the rite's true terms: the family must leave, but someone of keeper blood must remain inside to balance the ledger. He carries Mabel out through the breathing dark while the smiling things recite his name in his mother's voice. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing — survival or belonging, not both.

chapters.title: One
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV, final night. He sends the Vane family — Mabel's scattered descendants, summoned by letter — out past the threshold as the moon peaks. The count reaches one. Oscar steps inside and pulls the door shut behind him, sealing it from the inside as it was sealed before. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose; the nurse who wouldn't believe choosing to become the thing believed in.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Priya, POV, months later. No one in Hollowmere counts anymore. The excavation site is a meadow that blooms out of season. Priya visits the sealed door each equinox and tells Oscar the news — the town, the patients, the living. On zero, sometimes, she swears she hears him answer. Emotional beat: grief braided with peace; the price paid, the belonging earned.
